title: Identify and mitigate tail-root causes via preemptive request reshaping for embedding endpoint
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Embedding API p99 remains elevated for bursty traffic despite improvements to microbatch coalescing. Hypothesis: a small fraction of requests experience 'tail-root' delays caused by a combination of (1) last-byte GPU copy stalls for heterogeneous payload sizes, (2) kernel switchover penalties when sequence length distribution shifts, and (3) microbatch packing fragmentation. Goal: reduce embedding endpoint p99 by 25-40% for production traffic without regressing median latency or throughput. Approach: perform root-cause experiments, add lightweight preemptive request reshaping (split/merge strategy) to avoid kernel switchover and IO stalls, and add a guarded A/B rollout with metrics and canary throttles.
acceptance_criteria: Embedding endpoint p99 reduced by >=25% on production-like workload (measured on embeddings-prod-dashboard) compared to baseline from 2026-02-01
Median latency change within +/-5% of baseline
No >5% drop in aggregate throughput for dedicated and hosted tiers during canary rollout
Feature gate + rollout and rollback behave correctly (canary disabled within 5 minutes triggers rollback)
All code changes reviewed and have passing CI + perf tests (PR link in attachments)
implementation_steps: 1) Collect targeted traces: add fine-grained trace spans (ingress-arrival, batch-queue-wait, gpu-copy-start, kernel-select, kernel-exec, gpu-copy-end, response-serialize) for a 72h window
2) Offline tail-root analysis: run correlation between payload-size, seq-length, shard-assignment, and kernel-switch events to prioritize fixes
3) Prototype preemptive reshaping: implement reshape rules in microbatcher to split oversized requests into 'fastpath' chunks or coalesce small ones to avoid fragmentation
4) Kernel hinting: expose a kernel_hint field from scheduler to prefer stable kernels when sequence distribution uncertain
5) Add guarded scheduling: a short-lived speculative execution path that timeouts and falls back to normal batch path if delayed
6) Perf harness: run replay of production traces against canary runtime (quantized and fp16 variants) and collect p50/p95/p99
7) Canary rollout: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 25% with automatic rollback on metric degradation -> full rollout
8) Postmortem and docs: update embed runbook and console docs with new metrics and tuning knobs
notes: Trade-offs considered: speculative execution reduces tail but costs extra GPU ops; we limit speculative window to 30ms to bound cost impact
Reshaping rules must preserve ordering/semantics: embeddings are stateless so splitting is safe, but reranking pipeline downstream needs doc that chunking is transparent
We will start with a server-side feature flag and later expose a client opt-in if needed
Edge-case: extremely large single request (>1M tokens equivalent) will be rate-limited and surfaced as 413 until reshaping policy applied
